prompt: Provide an independent, technical diagnosis and fix plan for a self-contained offline HTML/JavaScript iPhone audio hum remover called HumLab. The user says 'Nothing works' when tapping downloaded HTML from ChatGPT on iPhone. User explicitly refuses Replit and wants a directly usable app. App must let them play/record a sample of noise to learn, import a recording, remove hum, audition before/after, and save cleaned audio. Identify delivery and implementation failures separately. Propose the most reliable no-Replit way to deliver a REAL functioning experience on iPhone, and how to test it. Crucially distinguish iOS Safari secure-context restrictions, sandboxed ChatGPT/Files HTML previews, local file:// restrictions, Web Audio autoplay/decode/file picker restrictions, and DSP weaknesses. Do not assume site deployment can be done merely by linking an HTML download. Provide a small reproducible acceptance-test matrix. Be candid if an app cannot run inline in ChatGPT. This is a READ ONLY consult; do not modify files.
context: Repository is user-owned GitHub repo maaronfanberg-lab/me- with GitHub Pages enabled, launcher at https://maaronfanberg-lab.github.io/me-/. The broken HumLab_Fixed.html is currently a downloaded sandbox HTML artifact, NOT published to GitHub Pages. User forbids Replit.

The HTML is 18.8 KB, one file, client-side script with DOM controls. Main file input: <input id='file' type='file' accept='audio/*,.wav,.mp3,.aac,.m4a,.mp4'>. On change: const b=await audioContext().decodeAudioData(await f.arrayBuffer()); source(b,URL.createObjectURL(f),f.name). Accepts <=35MB and <=180seconds. Reference file similar, allows select noise-only segment via two seconds inputs, 'Hear selected hum', 'Learn this hum'. 'Record hum' invokes navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia with echoCancellation/noiseSuppression/autoGainControl:false, MediaRecorder.isTypeSupported(['audio/mp4','audio/webm;codecs=opus','audio/webm']), uses MediaRecorder onstop to decode resulting Blob. If those APIs absent, prints access denied and suggests file option.

A 'Try a built-in demo' click creates two AudioBuffers at sampleRate 24000, four seconds of 60Hz+120Hz hum, plus a synthetic tone, serializes to WAV Blob/ObjectURL to load into <audio> playback. Processing button enabled when both source and reference loaded. DSP: FFT window length N=2048, hop H=512, sin window. Noise profile is average magnitude spectrum; STFT mask gain max(.12,1-1.55*strength*(scale*p[k])/(mag+.00001)), smoothing .45 previous + .55 new, inverse overlap-add. Additional notch biquad at estimated 50Hz vs 60Hz and harmonics 1..6 with Q=38. The profile p was measured at reference.sampleRate; processing applied to src.sampleRate WITHOUT resampling, causing incorrect frequency mapping if rates differ. WAV encoded to signed PCM 16-bit as Blob and downloadable objectURL. Two audio controls show 'before' 'after'. Secondary link with target=_blank opens audio URL for sharing on iPhone.

Potential issues: downloaded .html opens through Files Quick Look or ChatGPT sandbox preview, scripts may not run or sandbox restrictions inhibit file picker/mic and playback. Built-in desktop test was conducted only, no actual iPhone Safari test. Need distinguish code working in true browser from preview and recommend actual deployment, e.g. existing GitHub Pages, with no misleading claims. Source script uses optional chaining and modern browser features; a real hosted HTTPS origin is necessary for getUserMedia. UI has no recording of device playback loopback; user can play hum from another speaker into microphone or load a clip.

Advise prioritize a simple end-to-end sound import/demo/process/save experience before advanced DSP; actionable iPhone Safari quirks; how best to stage and validate using GitHub Pages. Do not claim you have executed the app or seen the user's device.
expected_response: Diagnosis ranked by likelihood; code-level issues including sample rates and quality; minimal corrective actions; robust no-Replit deployment approach on existing GitHub Pages; five concrete iPhone Safari acceptance tests; disclosure of unverified assumptions.
